title: What do angles three and six add up to?
description: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, and angle three is fifty degrees. A linear pair gives angle two, a corresponding angle gives angle six, and the two interior angles on the same side are added. Keeko doubts the answer, because Keeko thinks parallel lines make angles three and six equal.
teaching_notes: One idea: interior angles on the same side of a transversal of parallel lines add up to one hundred and eighty degrees. Watch for students who think angles three and six are equal.

source: Lines l and m are parallel and t is a transversal. The angle
video_script.why: The child chains a linear pair and a corresponding angle to find the interior angle on the same side, and sees that the two add up to a straight angle.
video_script.substitution: the book's own figure: parallel lines l and m, transversal t, angles 1 to 4 round the crossing with l and 5 to 8 in the same corners at m, angle 3 is fifty degrees
video_script.anchor: parallel lines l and m cut by the transversal t, with angles 1 to 4 round the crossing with l and 5 to 8 in the same corners at m, and angle 3 marked 50°
video_script.wrong_move: takes angles 3 and 6 to be equal because the lines are parallel
video_script.payoff_line: Interior angles on the same side always add up to one hundred and eighty

final_answer.value: Angle 6 = 130°; interior angles on the same side add to 180°
final_answer.spoken: angle six is one hundred and thirty degrees, and interior angles on the same side add up to one hundred and eighty degrees

hold_back: Angle 6 = 130°; interior angles on the same side add to 180°
maths_rules: angles 2 and 3 are a linear pair, so angle 2 = 180 - 50 = 130
angles 2 and 6 are corresponding angles of parallel lines, so angle 6 = 130
angles 3 and 6 are interior angles on the same side, and 50 + 130 = 180
for any angle 3: angle 3 + angle 2 = 180 and angle 2 = angle 6, so angle 3 + angle 6 = 180
video_script.design: One figure for the whole video. Angle three is in one colour and angle six in another, and a straight line is shown with the two of them adding up to a straight angle at the end.

narration: <bookmark mark='lin'/>Two angles side by side on a straight line are called a linear pair.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>A linear pair adds up to one hundred and eighty degrees.
<bookmark mark='corr'/>For parallel lines, angles in the same corner at the two crossings are equal.
<bookmark mark='int'/>Two angles between the lines on the same side of t are called interior angles.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks angle six is fifty, because the lines are parallel and parallel lines give equal angles.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But they give equal angles only in matching corners. Angles three and six are not in matching corners.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>They sit on the same side between the lines. They add up to one hundred and eighty degrees.
